statement: GPT-4o exhibits a 12.3% dosage hallucination rate on Spanish-language medical QA — significantly higher than the English baseline of 4.1% (χ²=27.4, p<0.001, n=1,200).
Chinese-language medical QA produces 2.8× more generic-name substitution errors compared to English across all evaluated models.
Claude Opus 4.1 shows the lowest cross-lingual hallucination variance (σ=0.031) across 7 evaluated languages.
dispute_note: Stats reviewer flagged the Arabic subset (n=48) as underpowered.

statement: Sampling temperature > 0.3 correlates with hallucination rate elevation across all models (ρ=0.71).
Retrieval-augmented generation reduces dosage hallucinations by ≥40% in Spanish and Portuguese.
Chain-of-thought prompting eliminates dosage hallucinations in medical QA.
refutation_note: Contradicted by experiment_run_01K5FZ8H — CoT increased over-confidence on wrong dosages.
